povRegister.registerSummary: Dry, exact, tactical. She thinks in footing, range, windows, counts, gear and horses; she reads people by hands, posture and kit. Her humor is contempt-dry and aimed at the Convocation and Lor'themar. She does not do thematic summary, confessional emotion-naming, or sympathy for the prisoner in this chapter.

findings.text: Most people, when she put her heels in, fell behind.
findings.issue: Paragraph-final closure. The paragraph already showed Lor'themar keeping pace ('stayed there, nose level with her stirrup', 'so he rode'). The closer explains the contrast the action carried.
findings.couldEndEarlierAt: sitting deep in the saddle as if this were what he'd intended all along.
findings.fixNote: DELETE the sentence. Paragraph ends on 'as if this were what he'd intended all along.'

findings.text: Two roads, and a body needed on each.
findings.issue: Thesis opening. The paragraph opens on a caption claim, then lays out the two roads in the next two sentences. The concrete sentences do the work; the opener is the topic sentence.
findings.fixNote: DELETE the sentence. Paragraph opens on 'Someone had to ride south, see this mage, and decide what she was.'

findings.text: He said nothing, wearing the same patient, far-too-knowing face he'd worn in the hollow with the troll-stink still on them.
findings.issue: Expression label as the whole beat. 'patient, far-too-knowing face' names the look with no physical sign. Also, no 'hollow' appears in Scene 1 (the earlier exchange happened over the dead troll at the gap, below the slope).
findings.suggestedFix: He said nothing. He only looked at her, head tilted, the way he had over the dead troll when she named the southern stones.

findings.text: With the Kirin Tor it was always worth considering both.
findings.issue: Restates what the reader already has. L159 already said 'with Dalaran, both was never out of the question.' Cutting it loses nothing.
findings.fixNote: DELETE the sentence. The paragraph ends on 'Or both.'

findings.text: one who'd simply been right in the wrong country
findings.deletionTest: one who'd been right in the wrong country
findings.issue: Hedge softener. Deleting 'simply' makes the line more direct. 'right in the wrong country' already marks this as the innocent option.
findings.suggestedFix: one who'd been right in the wrong country

findings.text: She had put it away the moment Sylvanas filled the doorway. Whether that was sense or pride, Sylvanas couldn't tell yet.
findings.issue: Interpretive restatement. L287 already showed it: 'Then she closed her mouth on whatever she'd meant to say.' 'She had put it away the moment Sylvanas filled the doorway' says it again. The cited span includes the next sentence only because its 'that' points back to the cut line.
findings.suggestedFix: Whether swallowing it now was sense or pride, Sylvanas couldn't tell yet.

findings.issue: Paragraph-final emotional summary. It names the curiosity that the open sense-or-pride question already carries. The paragraph is stronger ending on 'couldn't tell yet.'
findings.couldEndEarlierAt: Whether ... sense or pride, Sylvanas couldn't tell yet.

findings.text: The woman had spent the afternoon chained to a floor while a barley pot burned next door and the stones she'd come to read stood on the hillside without her.
findings.whoIsSayingThis: A narrator summarizing the prisoner's day from outside.
findings.povMismatch: A standalone paragraph that pulls back to recap facts the reader already has (irons, barley pot, stones), framed through what the prisoner wanted ('the stones she'd come to read stood on the hillside without her'). That sympathetic framing works against the plan's no-warmth lock and Sylvanas's register in the doorway read.
findings.fixNote: DELETE the paragraph. L289 flows straight into 'Cyndia came up at her shoulder...'

findings.text: It was one of the more irritating things about serving beside someone for longer than most human kingdoms had existed.
findings.whoIsSayingThis: A narrator generalizing ('serving beside someone') over the specific moment with Lor'themar.
findings.povMismatch: Moves from this exchange up to a category claim about long service. It is a paragraph-final essay zoom, not an active thought.
findings.suggestedFix: He had been doing that to her for longer than most human kingdoms had existed.

findings.text: Most people, when she put her heels in, fell behind.
findings.whoIsSayingThis: A narrator setting Lor'themar against 'most people'.
findings.povMismatch: A generalization made to decorate the moment, not a tactical conclusion that drives an action. Same sentence as B-G1 (F7). One fix covers both.
findings.fixNote: DELETE the sentence (same fix as B-G1).

findings.text: It was harder now than it had been an hour ago, under the gold, to check one and move on, because a stranger had knelt at stones like these this morning and called what lay under them wrong.
findings.missingPayload: What 'harder' looks like: what she does differently at each stone. The page shows her checking 'foot to crown', not lingering or hesitating.
findings.suggestedFix: She lingered at each one longer than she had under the gold, because a stranger had knelt at stones like these this morning and called what lay under them wrong.

findings.text: "The Convocation always wants to have known first. It's the knowing that tires them."
findings.failedQuestion: What does this cash out to?
findings.missingPayload: The plain claim behind 'the knowing': the Convocation wants credit for being told first, then wants someone else to handle the prisoner. If Lor'themar asked 'Tires them how?', the line has no answer.
findings.suggestedFix: "The Convocation always wants to have known first. Then it wants us to handle her."

audits.cleanReason: No speaker asks for plainer speech, smaller words, or 'streets'. Four near-setups were audited as exchanges. (1) L113-117 'Report.' / Theris's clipped report gives usable payload: first ring, rocks east of the road, before dawn, taken at the second ring an hour past sunup, kneeling, book, no papers. (2) L127-131 'Wrong how?' / 'She didn't say. Or she said, and none of us could follow it.' Theris admits he cannot translate rather than faking a translation. (3) L245-247 'Theris says what she says. This is me.' Cyndia's plain-speech recast names the stone, the method (palms, as the magisters taught at Fairbreeze), the sign (reads like a cracked stone with no mark; a full cask answering hollow), and the count (six since noon, second ring and first). That is a usable target and a usable trigger. (4) L161-165 Sylvanas's briefing to Lor'themar gives exact content to deliver and an exact limit ('Tell them she said it. Not that it's true.').
